title: A Bed of Thorns
summary: A servant naps on the king’s soft bed and gets slapped. He laughs, then cries, saying the bed must bring a king many worries. The king agrees it is a bed of thorns.
levelReason: The supplied text uses formal words (luxurious, responsibilities, governing, expedition, privileges), long complex sentences, and an abstract moral about power and responsibility, which matches Level 3.

en: A king of Srirangapatnam went hunting in the forest. While he was away, his servant Nanjayya came to clean the king’s bedroom.
Nanjayya saw the king’s big bed. It looked so soft. The sheets were fine. The pillows were the best he had ever seen.
He wondered how it would feel to sleep there. He looked around. Nobody was watching. “Just for a few minutes,” he thought, and he lay down.
The pillow was so soft. Nanjayya felt calm and happy. He forgot his work. Soon he was fast asleep.
Then the king came home from hunting. He walked into his room. He was shocked. Nanjayya was asleep on the royal bed!
The king was very angry. He went to the servant and shook him awake. Then he slapped him hard.
Nanjayya opened his eyes. The king was surprised. First the servant laughed. Then he began to cry.
The king did not understand. “Why did you laugh? And why did you cry right after?” he asked.
Nanjayya answered with respect. “Your Majesty, I laughed because I got to sleep on your soft bed, even for a few minutes.”
The king listened. “But why did you cry?” he asked.

“I cried because this bed must give you many troubles, Your Majesty. I slept here for a few minutes, and I got a painful slap. But you sleep here every night, with all the worries of the whole kingdom.”
The king said nothing. Nanjayya went on. “A royal bed may look soft, but the one who sleeps on it has many worries. The more duties a person has, the harder it is to enjoy even the best things.”
The king was moved by these words. Nanjayya understood something many people miss. A king may have gold, palaces and fine things. But he must also look after his people and his land.
The king smiled. “You are right, Nanjayya. A king’s bed is not a bed of roses. It is a bed of thorns. I sleep on silk, but my mind is always busy with my people.”
The king forgave Nanjayya and let him go back to work. Nanjayya left with a new understanding of how heavy a leader’s duties are. And the king remembered that even a humble servant can be wise.
Moral: Money and comfort do not always bring happiness. Big privileges come with big duties.
hi: श्रीरंगपट्टनम का एक राजा जंगल में शिकार करने गया। उसके पीछे उसका सेवक नंजय्या राजा का शयनकक्ष साफ़ करने आया।
नंजय्या ने राजा का बड़ा पलंग देखा। वह बहुत नरम लग रहा था। चादरें बढ़िया थीं। तकिए सबसे अच्छे थे जो उसने कभी देखे थे।
उसने सोचा कि वहाँ सोना कैसा लगेगा। उसने इधर-उधर देखा। कोई नहीं देख रहा था। “बस कुछ मिनट,” उसने सोचा, और लेट गया।
तकिया बहुत नरम था। नंजय्या को शांति और खुशी हुई। वह अपना काम भूल गया। जल्दी ही वह गहरी नींद में सो गया।
तभी राजा शिकार से घर लौटा। वह अपने कमरे में गया। वह चौंक गया। नंजय्या शाही पलंग पर सो रहा था!
राजा को बहुत गुस्सा आया। वह सेवक के पास गया और उसे झकझोरकर जगाया। फिर उसने ज़ोर से थप्पड़ मारा।
नंजय्या ने आँखें खोलीं। राजा हैरान हुआ। पहले सेवक हँसा। फिर वह रोने लगा।
राजा को समझ नहीं आया। “तुम हँसे क्यों? और फिर तुरंत रोए क्यों?” उसने पूछा।
नंजय्या ने आदर से कहा। “महाराज, मैं इसलिए हँसा कि मुझे आपके नरम पलंग पर सोने को मिला, चाहे कुछ ही मिनट।”
राजा ने सुना। “पर तुम रोए क्यों?” उसने पूछा।
“मैं इसलिए रोया कि इस पलंग से आपको बहुत परेशानियाँ होती होंगी, महाराज। मैं यहाँ कुछ मिनट सोया और मुझे दर्द देने वाला थप्पड़ मिला। पर आप हर रात यहाँ सोते हैं, पूरे राज्य की चिंताओं के साथ।”

राजा कुछ नहीं बोला। नंजय्या ने आगे कहा। “शाही पलंग नरम दिखता है, पर उस पर सोने वाले को बहुत चिंताएँ होती हैं। जिसके पास जितने ज़्यादा काम होते हैं, उसके लिए अच्छी चीज़ों का मज़ा लेना उतना ही कठिन होता है।”
राजा इन बातों से बहुत प्रभावित हुआ। नंजय्या ने वह बात समझी थी जो बहुत लोग नहीं समझते। राजा के पास सोना, महल और सुंदर चीज़ें हो सकती हैं। पर उसे अपनी प्रजा और अपने देश का ध्यान भी रखना होता है।
राजा मुस्कुराया। “तुम ठीक कहते हो, नंजय्या। राजा का पलंग फूलों की सेज नहीं है। यह काँटों की सेज है। मैं रेशम पर सोता हूँ, पर मेरा मन हमेशा अपनी प्रजा की चिंता में रहता है।”
राजा ने नंजय्या को माफ़ कर दिया और उसे काम पर लौटने दिया। नंजय्या यह समझकर गया कि नेता की ज़िम्मेदारी कितनी भारी होती है। और राजा को याद आया कि एक साधारण सेवक भी समझदार हो सकता है।
सीख: पैसा और आराम हमेशा सुख नहीं देते। बड़े अधिकारों के साथ बड़ी ज़िम्मेदारियाँ आती हैं।

en: Once, the king of Srirangapatnam went hunting in the forest. While he was away, his servant Nanjayya went into the royal bedchamber to clean it.
As he worked, he noticed the king’s magnificent bed. It looked wonderfully soft, with fine sheets and pillows more luxurious than any Nanjayya had ever seen.
He wondered what it would feel like to sleep on such a bed. After checking that nobody was watching, he decided to lie down for just a few minutes.
The moment his head touched the soft pillow, he felt completely relaxed. The bed was so comfortable that he forgot his work, and before long he was fast asleep.
Meanwhile, the king came back from his hunt. When he walked into his bedroom, he was amazed to find Nanjayya sleeping peacefully on the royal bed.
The king was furious. He walked up to the servant, shook him awake and slapped him hard.
Nanjayya opened his eyes. To the king’s surprise, the servant first laughed and then began to cry.
The king was puzzled. “Why did you laugh when I woke you, and why did you start crying right after?” he demanded.
Nanjayya replied respectfully, “Your Majesty, I laughed because I had the pleasure of sleeping on your wonderfully soft bed, even if only for a few minutes.”
The king listened. “But why did you cry?” he asked.

Nanjayya answered, “I cried because I realised that this beautiful bed must bring you many troubles. I enjoyed it for only a few minutes and was punished with a painful slap. But you must spend every night on it, carrying the worries and duties of the whole kingdom.”

The king stayed silent, and Nanjayya continued. “Your Majesty, a royal bed may look comfortable, but the person sleeping on it must have many worries. The more responsibilities one carries, the harder it is to enjoy even the greatest comforts.”

The king was deeply impressed. He saw that Nanjayya had understood something many people miss. A king may have great wealth, beautiful palaces and fine things, but he also carries the heavy duty of protecting his people and ruling the kingdom.
The king smiled and said, “You are right, Nanjayya. A king’s bed is not a bed of roses. It is a bed of thorns. I may sleep on silk, but my mind is always busy with the welfare of my people.”

He forgave the servant and let him go back to his work. Nanjayya left the room with a new understanding of the burdens of leadership. And the king was reminded that even a humble servant can offer great wisdom.
Moral: Wealth and luxury do not always bring happiness. Great responsibilities often come with great privileges.

en: Once upon a time, the king of Srirangapatnam went hunting in the forest. While the king was away, his servant Nanjayya entered the royal bedchamber to clean it.

As he worked, his eyes fell upon the king’s magnificent bed. It looked incredibly soft and comfortable. The mattress was covered with fine sheets, and the pillows appeared more luxurious than anything Nanjayya had ever seen.
He wondered what it would feel like to sleep on such a wonderful bed. After looking around to make sure nobody was watching, he decided to lie down for just a few minutes.
The moment he rested his head on the soft pillow, he felt completely relaxed. The bed was so comfortable that he soon forgot about his work. Before long, he had fallen fast asleep.
Meanwhile, the king returned from his hunting expedition. When he entered his bedroom, he was astonished to find Nanjayya sleeping peacefully on his royal bed.
The king was furious. He walked towards the servant, shook him awake and slapped him hard.
Nanjayya opened his eyes. To the king’s surprise, the servant first laughed and then began to cry.
The king was puzzled. “Why did you laugh when I woke you, and why did you begin crying immediately afterwards?” he demanded.
Nanjayya respectfully replied: “Your Majesty, I laughed because I had the pleasure of sleeping on your wonderfully soft bed, even if only for a few minutes.”
The king listened. “But why did you cry?” he asked.

Nanjayya answered: “I cried because I realised that this beautiful bed must bring you many troubles. I enjoyed its comfort for only a few minutes and was immediately punished with a painful slap. You, however, must spend every night on this bed, carrying the worries and responsibilities of the entire kingdom.”

The king remained silent. Nanjayya continued: “Your Majesty, I now understand that a royal bed may look comfortable, but the person sleeping on it must have many worries. The more responsibilities one carries, the more difficult it becomes to enjoy even the greatest comforts.”

The king was deeply impressed by the servant’s words. He realised that Nanjayya had understood something that many people failed to recognise. A king might possess great wealth, beautiful palaces and luxurious possessions, but he also carried the enormous responsibility of protecting his people and governing the kingdom.

The king smiled and said: “You are right, Nanjayya. A king’s bed is not a bed of roses. It is a bed of thorns. I may sleep on silk, but my mind is constantly occupied with the welfare of my subjects.”

He forgave the servant and allowed him to return to his duties. Nanjayya left the chamber with a new understanding of the burdens of leadership. And the king, too, was reminded that even a humble servant could offer great wisdom.
Moral: Wealth and luxury do not necessarily bring happiness. Great responsibilities often accompany great privileges.

नंजय्या ने कहा: “मैं इसलिए रोया कि मुझे समझ आया कि यह सुंदर पलंग आपको बहुत परेशानियाँ देता होगा। मैंने इसके आराम का आनंद बस कुछ मिनट लिया और तुरंत एक दर्दभरे थप्पड़ की सज़ा पाई। पर आपको तो हर रात इसी पलंग पर सोना है, और पूरे राज्य की चिंताओं और ज़िम्मेदारियों का बोझ उठाना है।”

राजा चुप रहा। नंजय्या ने आगे कहा: “महाराज, अब मैं समझता हूँ कि शाही पलंग देखने में आरामदायक लगे, पर उस पर सोने वाले को बहुत चिंताएँ होती हैं। जितनी अधिक ज़िम्मेदारियाँ कोई उठाता है, उतना ही कठिन हो जाता है बड़े से बड़े सुखों का आनंद लेना।”

राजा सेवक की बातों से गहराई तक प्रभावित हुआ। उसने महसूस किया कि नंजय्या ने वह बात समझ ली है जिसे बहुत से लोग नहीं पहचान पाते। एक राजा के पास अपार धन, सुंदर महल और ऐशो-आराम की चीज़ें हो सकती हैं, पर उस पर अपनी प्रजा की रक्षा करने और राज्य चलाने की भारी ज़िम्मेदारी भी होती है।
राजा मुस्कुराया और बोला: “तुम ठीक कहते हो, नंजय्या। राजा का पलंग फूलों की सेज नहीं है। यह काँटों की सेज है। मैं रेशम पर सोता हूँ, पर मेरा मन हर समय अपनी प्रजा की भलाई की चिंता में लगा रहता है।”
उसने सेवक को माफ़ कर दिया और उसे अपने काम पर लौटने दिया। नंजय्या नेतृत्व के बोझ की एक नई समझ लेकर कमरे से निकला। और राजा को भी याद आया कि एक साधारण सेवक भी बड़ी समझदारी की बात कह सकता है।
सीख: धन और ऐशो-आराम से सुख मिले, यह ज़रूरी नहीं। बड़े अधिकारों के साथ अक्सर बड़ी ज़िम्मेदारियाँ भी आती हैं।

duties you are expected to carry out

questions.q: Nanjayya broke a rule, and the king slapped him. Was either action fair? What would a just response have been?
How might the story look from the king’s point of view, with his worries? And from the point of view of other servants?
This is a folk tale about a king, a servant and a wise answer. Why might many cultures enjoy stories where a humble person teaches a ruler?
The moral says responsibilities come with privileges. Do you agree? Who carries such burdens today?
Do leaders, parents or teachers today also carry worries we do not see? How should we treat them and each other?

scenes.p: King: a middle-aged man with a trimmed moustache, a rich maroon silk turban with a gold brooch, a cream silk coat with gold border, simple jewellery. Nanjayya: a lean young servant with a plain white head-cloth and white dhoti, bare feet, a kind face. The royal bed: a carved wooden bed with a silk mattress, white sheets and plump pillows. Nanjayya, with a broom and cloth, admires the grand royal bed in a sunny palace bedchamber; a window shows the king riding off. Warm, curious mood.

artStyle.note: Karnataka Tourism describes Mysore painting as a style from the Wodeyar courts, with refined delicate lines, natural mineral colours, gold-leaf detail and figures framed by arches. We suggest borrowing this soft palette and fine gold-trimmed borders for the palace scenes. This is a style suggestion only; no source ties this story to it. Keep the slap non-graphic.

imagine: Imagine you can lie on the king’s bed for one minute. What do you feel, and what do you think about while the palace is quiet?
create: Draw the king’s bed in two ways: one as it looks from outside, and one as the king feels it at night. Write one sentence for each.

about.where: Srirangapatna (Srirangapatnam in the story) is a town in Mandya district, Karnataka, on an island in the Kaveri River about 15 km from Mysuru. It was an important capital of the Mysore kingdom and is known for the Sri Ranganathaswamy temple.
about.community: The sources we have do not say which community first told this version, so we are not guessing. The repository says the tale comes from a published collection of Karnataka folk tales.
about.tradition: Folk tales of a wise servant who speaks plainly to a king are told in many places. Karnataka’s royal courts, such as the Wodeyars of Mysuru, also supported arts like Mysore painting.
about.shared: The tale uses a clever answer to teach a lesson, a pattern found in many folk traditions. Here the king listens, forgives, and learns.
about.matters: The story asks us to look beyond how things appear: a life of comfort may carry heavy duties. It is one version from one source, not the only one.
